Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act

federal_reports.title: The Problem of Indian Administration (Meriam Report)
federal_reports.author: Lewis Meriam et al.
federal_reports.description: First major federal survey documenting catastrophic poverty, disease, and educational failure in Indian communities caused by allotment and boarding school policy.

federal_reports.title: Indian Education: A National Tragedy — A National Challenge (Kennedy Report)
federal_reports.author: Senate Special Subcommittee on Indian Education
federal_reports.description: Documented systematic failure of federal and public schools to educate Indian children. Called for tribal community control of Indian education.

federal_reports.title: A Quiet Crisis: Federal Funding and Unmet Needs in Indian Country
federal_reports.author: U.S. Commission on Civil Rights
federal_reports.description: Documented systematic federal underfunding of Indian health, education, and housing programs relative to non-Indian equivalents.

census_materials.title: U.S. Census Records 1790–1960 (American Indian Enumeration)
census_materials.description: Primary source for tracing census racial classification of Indian families. Enumerator instructions from each decade show policy-driven reclassification.

census_materials.title: 2020 Census American Indian and Alaska Native Population
census_materials.description: Shows 39% increase in American Indian self-identification from 2010 — documenting recovery from decades of under-reporting, not population growth.

state_records.title: Virginia Bureau of Vital Statistics Records (Walter Plecker Era)
state_records.description: Birth, death, and marriage records from Virginia showing systematic reclassification of Indian families as 'colored' under Plecker's administration.

health_policy.title: Urban Indian Health: A Review of the Literature
health_policy.author: Urban Indian Health Institute
health_policy.description: Comprehensive review documenting health disparities for urban Indians and the gap in federal health services between reservation and urban populations.

health_policy.title: Invisible Tribes: Urban Indians and Their Health in a Changing World
health_policy.author: Urban Indian Health Institute
health_policy.description: Documents how urban Indians are systematically excluded from federal health data, making their health needs invisible to policymakers.

urban_indian_policy.title: Gathering of Voices for the Native Communities
urban_indian_policy.author: Urban Indian Health Institute
urban_indian_policy.description: Community health assessment documenting the needs and conditions of urban Indian communities in major cities.

urban_indian_policy.title: Urban Indian Statistics
urban_indian_policy.author: National Council of Urban Indian Health
urban_indian_policy.description: Current statistics on urban Indian population, health, and service access.

court_cases.title: Worcester v. Georgia
court_cases.description: States have no authority over Indian nations. Federal-tribal relationship is nation-to-nation. Still controlling law.

court_cases.title: Passamaquoddy Tribe v. Morton
court_cases.description: Federal trust responsibility extends to tribes not on BIA administrative recognition list. Being 'unrecognized' does not eliminate trust rights.

court_cases.title: Morton v. Mancari
court_cases.description: Indian status is a political, not racial, classification. Federal Indian preference programs are not racial discrimination.

court_cases.title: Cobell v. Salazar
court_cases.description: $3.4 billion settlement for federal mismanagement of Individual Indian Money trust accounts since 1887.

court_cases.title: Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo
court_cases.description: Chevron deference overturned. Agency interpretations of Indian law statutes are now subject to independent judicial review.

treaties.title: Treaty of Hopewell (Cherokee)
treaties.description: First treaty between the United States and the Cherokee Nation. Established boundaries and mutual obligations. Signed November 28, 1785 at Hopewell, South Carolina.

treaties.title: Treaty of Hopewell (Choctaw)
treaties.description: Treaty between the United States and the Choctaw Nation. Signed January 3, 1786. Established peace and boundaries in the Choctaw homeland of present-day Mississippi and Alabama.

treaties.title: Treaty of Hopewell (Chickasaw)
treaties.description: Treaty between the United States and the Chickasaw Nation. Signed January 10, 1786. Established Chickasaw territorial boundaries in northern Mississippi and western Tennessee.

treaties.title: Treaty of Holston (Cherokee)
treaties.description: Established peace, boundaries, and US citizenship protections for Cherokee people. Signed July 2, 1791 at the Holston River.

treaties.title: Treaty of Canandaigua (Six Nations / Haudenosaunee)
treaties.description: Treaty with the Six Nations of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy (Iroquois). Signed November 11, 1794. Defined boundaries and preserved Haudenosaunee sovereignty within New York. Annuity payments continue today.

treaties.title: Treaty of Fort Pitt (Lenape / Delaware)
treaties.description: The first formal treaty between the United States and an Indigenous nation. Signed September 17, 1778 with the Lenape (Delaware) Nation at Fort Pitt. Established alliance during the Revolutionary War.

treaties.title: Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek (Choctaw)
treaties.description: First removal treaty under the Indian Removal Act. Signed September 27, 1830. The Choctaw ceded all remaining lands east of the Mississippi in exchange for lands in Indian Territory and citizenship protections — many of which the US failed to honor.

treaties.title: Treaty of New Echota (Cherokee)
treaties.description: Negotiated by an unauthorized minority faction without authority from the Cherokee National Council. Ceded all Cherokee lands east of the Mississippi. Principal Chief John Ross and 15,000 Cherokee signed a protest petition. Used by the US government to justify the Trail of Tears (1838–1839).

treaties.title: Treaty of Cusseta (Creek / Muscogee)
treaties.description: Signed March 24, 1832. Allotted Creek lands in Alabama in individual parcels, paving the way for fraudulent sales and forced removal. Led directly to the Creek Removal (1836–1837).

treaties.title: Treaty of Pontotoc Creek (Chickasaw)
treaties.description: Signed October 20, 1832. The Chickasaw ceded their homeland in northern Mississippi and western Tennessee. The Chickasaw negotiated more favorable removal terms than other Five Civilized Tribes.

treaties.title: Treaty of Payne's Landing (Seminole)
treaties.description: Contested removal treaty with the Seminole Nation. Many Seminole leaders repudiated it. Its enforcement triggered the Second Seminole War (1835–1842), the costliest and longest US-Indian war.

treaties.title: Fort Laramie Treaty (1851)
treaties.description: Recognized the territories of Lakota, Cheyenne, Arapaho, Crow, Assiniboine, Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara nations on the Northern Plains. Established peace and defined territorial boundaries.

treaties.title: Fort Laramie Treaty (1868)
treaties.description: Established the Great Sioux Reservation including the Black Hills (He Sapa) as unceded Lakota territory. Required three-fourths consent of adult male tribal members for any land modifications. Broken by the US government in 1877 when gold was discovered. The Supreme Court ruled the 1877 seizure illegal in US v. Sioux Nation (1980).

treaties.title: Treaty of Bosque Redondo / Navajo Treaty of 1868
treaties.description: Allowed the Diné (Navajo) people to return to their homeland after four years of imprisonment at Bosque Redondo. Established the Navajo Reservation in the Four Corners region — one of the few treaties that allowed a nation to return to its homeland rather than relocate.

treaties.title: Medicine Lodge Treaty (1867)
treaties.description: Signed with the Comanche, Kiowa, Kiowa-Apache, Cheyenne, and Arapaho nations. Established reservations in Indian Territory (Oklahoma) and promised annuities and education. Violations of its terms led to the Red River War (1874–1875).

treaties.title: Yakama Treaty (1855)
treaties.description: Signed June 9, 1855 with the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation. Preserved treaty rights to fish, hunt, and gather at all usual and accustomed places — rights repeatedly affirmed by federal courts through the 20th century.

treaties.title: Treaty of Point Elliott (1855)
treaties.description: Signed January 22, 1855 with Coast Salish peoples (Lummi, Suquamish, Tulalip, Swinomish, and others). Reserved fishing rights at usual and accustomed places, affirmed in United States v. Washington (Boldt Decision, 1974).

treaties.title: Kappler's Indian Affairs: Laws and Treaties (Complete Edition)
treaties.author: Charles J. Kappler, Senate Document
treaties.description: The comprehensive compilation of all US-Indian treaties and laws, compiled by Senate law librarian Charles J. Kappler. The authoritative reference for treaty text, dates, and citations. Volumes I–VII cover treaties (1778–1883), statutes, executive orders, and proclamations.

maps.title: Native Land Digital — Treaty and Territory Maps
maps.description: Interactive map of Indigenous territories, treaties, and languages.

maps.title: Indian Land Cessions in the United States — Charles C. Royce
maps.author: Charles C. Royce, Bureau of American Ethnology
maps.citation: 18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, Part 2 (1899)
maps.description: The definitive cartographic record of every treaty-based Indian land cession in the United States, compiled by the Bureau of American Ethnology. Includes 67 maps and a schedule of all land cession treaties from colonial era through 1894. The primary scholarly and legal reference for documenting which lands were ceded under which treaty.
